title: Terracotta Kitchen Wall Tiles: Ideas That Handle Heat and Splashes
excerpt: How terracotta kitchen wall tiles cope with heat, oil and splashes, where to use them, and when a glazed tile is the better choice.
meta_title: Terracotta Kitchen Wall Tiles: Heat and Splash Guide
meta_description: Can terracotta kitchen wall tiles handle heat, oil and splashes? How to seal, place and clean clay tiles in a Pakistani kitchen, plus glazed alternatives.
answer_box: Terracotta kitchen wall tiles are fired-clay tiles used as a backsplash or feature wall. Clay tolerates cooking heat, but it is porous and can absorb oil, so natural tiles usually need a sealer, while a glazed tile is often wiser directly behind the stove.
ai_summary: Terracotta kitchen wall tiles tolerate cooking heat, but natural clay is porous and can absorb oil and splashes, so it usually needs sealing and careful placement. A glazed tile is often wiser right behind the hob. Pak Clay, a Lahore clay tile maker since 1982, offers a free sample you can test in your own kitchen.
author: Pak Clay Team

faqs.question: Can terracotta tiles handle heat behind a stove?
faqs.answer: Fired clay generally tolerates cooking heat. The weak points are usually the adhesive and grout, so ask your fixer for kitchen-suitable materials and follow the product's guidance near open flames.

faqs.question: Do terracotta kitchen tiles stain from oil?
faqs.answer: Natural terracotta is porous and can absorb oil and spices. A sealer helps, or you can use a glazed tile in the splash zone. Test a sample with oil and water before you commit.

faqs.question: Should I choose terracotta or glazed mosaic for a kitchen wall?
faqs.answer: Glazed tiles usually wipe clean more easily; terracotta gives a natural, earthy look but needs sealing. Many kitchens use glazed behind the hob and terracotta elsewhere.
